binomial distribution|binomial: the distribution of $X$ = the number of successes in $n$ independent trials with the same probability $p$ of success on each; $P(x) = {}_nC_x\,p^x\,q^{n-x}$, $\mu = np$, $\sigma = \sqrt{npq}$. See [Binomial on paper](#/math3042-q7/binomial-on-paper).
Poisson distribution|Poisson: the distribution of $X$ = the number of events in a fixed interval of time or space when the average number per interval is $\lambda$; $P(x) = \lambda^x e^{-\lambda}/x!$, $\mu = \lambda$, $\sigma = \sqrt{\lambda}$. See [Poisson on paper](#/math3042-q7/poisson-on-paper).
lambda|λ: the mean number of events in the interval the question asks about: the rate times the length of that interval. See [Poisson on paper](#/math3042-q7/poisson-on-paper).
complement: the event that something does not happen; $P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - P(\text{none})$. See [At least, at most, more than](#/math3042-q7/at-least-at-most).
cumulative probability: $P(X \le k)$, the sum of $P(0)$ to $P(k)$; R's `pbinom(k, n, p)` and `ppois(k, lambda)`. See [At least, at most, more than](#/math3042-q7/at-least-at-most).
unusual: a value more than two standard deviations from the mean: $|Z| > 2$ with $Z = (x - \mu)/\sigma$. See [Binomial on paper](#/math3042-q7/binomial-on-paper).
logical vector|logical column: a column of TRUE/FALSE values made by a comparison such as `survey$Smoke != "Never"`; `sum()` counts the TRUEs and `mean()` gives their proportion. See [Working with data in RStudio](#/math3042-q7/r-data-moves).
conditional probability: $P(A \mid B)$, the proportion of the rows where $B$ is TRUE in which $A$ is also TRUE: `sum(A & B)/sum(B)`. See [Probabilities from a data frame](#/math3042-q7/r-probabilities-from-data).
mutually exclusive: two events that cannot both happen: `sum(A & B)` is 0. See [Probabilities from a data frame](#/math3042-q7/r-probabilities-from-data).
independent events|independent: events where $P(A \mid B) = P(A)$, equivalently $P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B)$. See [Probabilities from a data frame](#/math3042-q7/r-probabilities-from-data).
na.rm: an argument of `mean()` and `sum()` that drops missing values (NA) before computing; without it a single NA makes the answer NA. See [Probabilities from a data frame](#/math3042-q7/r-probabilities-from-data).
dbinom|pbinom|rbinom: R's binomial functions: `dbinom(x, size, prob)` is $P(X = x)$, `pbinom(q, size, prob)` is $P(X \le q)$, `rbinom(n, size, prob)` draws $n$ random values. See [dbinom, pbinom, dpois, ppois](#/math3042-q7/r-binomial-poisson).
dpois|ppois|rpois: R's Poisson functions: `dpois(x, lambda)` is $P(X = x)$, `ppois(q, lambda)` is $P(X \le q)$, `rpois(n, lambda)` draws $n$ random values. See [dbinom, pbinom, dpois, ppois](#/math3042-q7/r-binomial-poisson).
nCx|combination: the number of ways to choose which $x$ of the $n$ trials are the successes, ${}_nC_x = n!/(x!\,(n-x)!)$; the calculator's nCr key, R's choose(n, x). See [Before you start](#/math3042-q7/pre-reading).
knit: RStudio's button that re-runs every chunk of the notebook from the top in a fresh session and writes the Word file Part 2 is marked on.
